key_idea: Split the problem in two using the hexagon-with-centre graph H: one gadget (L) forces some copy of H to have a monochromatic √3-triple in every 4-colouring, and another gadget (M) forbids that triple. Then glue copies of M onto every copy of H in L.
reason: The gadget idea has a clear conceptual skeleton, and the rotation tricks by 2·arcsin(1/4) and 2·arcsin(1/8) are clever. But the decisive step is a 1345-vertex graph found by computer search and checked by backtracking, and the final certificate is SAT-verified, so a human cannot survey why the result holds.
recognized: de Grey, 'The chromatic number of the plane is at least 5' (2018)
